text: 6.2 This is Andrew Thompson reporting from the Spanish island of El Iero about 400 kilometers off the coast of Africa. It's pretty far from Madrid which is about 2000 kilometers away. Today we're going to talk to two of the 11,000 people who live here to find out what's so special about the island. First, this is Pedro Rodríquez who owns a seafood restaurant on the island. Hello Pedro. Hello Andrew. So, how long have you lived on El Iero? I haven't lived here for very long. I came from Madrid about five years ago. You don't like it here then? I love it here. I wish I had come a lot sooner than I did. I spent a lot of my life in Madrid. City life can be tough. I suppose island life is rather more relaxing. El Iero is my home now. So, what's so great about El Iero? In the city, everyone has everywhere. You are surrounded by traffic. You never feel like you can really relax. Was more, my career was in banking, which is a particularly stressful job. I love the sound of the sea. I love the peace and quiet. And I feel free here. City life was never like that. When I was living in the city, I worked in banking, as I said. It paid well. And I was able to buy my restaurant. But I should have left the city when I was a much younger man. So you love the quiet life on El Iero. But is there anything else that makes El Iero special? Well, another thing is, El Iero is completely energy independent. Energy independent? Yes. In the past, the power on the island was produced by oil. A lot of money was paid to ship 40,000 barrels of oil over from the mainland every year. It cost the island over 1.7 million euros a year. Now all our energy is created right here on the island.
